Author: Midona
Name: Poser
Punchline: Posing, lighting and whole-scene staging for group pose. Beta.
Description:
Poser is a posing and scene tool for FINAL FANTASY XIV's group pose.

- Pose actors bone by bone: overlay handles, a graphical body map, and numeric transforms
- IK on any bone with a parent, plus mirror, link and named bone-visibility presets
- Spawn actors and objects, or click a world handle to bring what is already there into the scene
- Borrow the map's own objects by reference and give them back untouched on release
- Save and restore the whole shot — actors, objects, lights, camera and environment — with load options
- Custom lights, camera control and a free camera; snapping, group pivot and group moves
- Gaze control and one-click expressions
- A pose library with tags, authors and search; import and export poses, and MCDF appearance files
- Time, weather and festival control
- On-screen dialogue panels, chat bubbles and status lines drawn with the game's own UI
- Reference pictures as floating, aspect-locked windows
- Twenty-five rebindable actions with Poser, Brio and Ktisis presets

This is a beta. It is not stable and it is not finished. Poser is derivative of Anamnesis, Ktisis and Brio, and those three are the mature tools.

Poser was coded with the use of artificial intelligence. The plugin says so on first launch and asks you to confirm you have read the notice.
Changelog:
- After an actor is removed and the removal is undone, undo and redo of that actor's earlier changes reach it again: appearance, colours, opacity, gaze, animation, face sliders, IK settings and bakes, equipment, Customize, Reset All and companions.
- The camera keeps following an actor after its removal is undone, even when another actor took its place in the meantime.
- Groups keep the right members, and their position, rotation and scale, after a member's removal is undone.
- Undoing the removal of a copy with an MCDF applied gives the copy its own mods back.
- A second undo while an actor is still coming back waits with a message instead of acting on the wrong actor.
- Reset → All no longer sits the actor back down after Sit was played and the stance was then changed.
- Applying an emote to a seated actor plays the seated version and keeps the actor seated.
- Undoing a sitting stance keeps the actor seated.
- Undo puts back the speed of a layer the game was playing.
- The camera turn an emote causes is no longer recorded as a camera move.
- A hand that follows another actor's head or hand follows it in the same frame, including when the two actors follow each other.
- A chain that follows a bone of its own actor, such as one hand following the other, picks up that bone's own edits.
- IK collisions against a collider on another actor's bone follow that actor's pose.
- IK chains are kept when an actor is redrawn.
- Lock stops moving, rotating and scaling only.
- Removing an actor with a minion attached works, and so does Set collection on that minion.
- An actor's opacity is kept when it is hidden and shown again.
- Scenes save and load each actor's gaze.
- A light keeps its old gobo when the game refuses a new one.
- Deleting or renaming a file updates the Library list straight away.
- A failed MCDF from the Library says why it failed.
- A pose file that can't be read says why.
- The auto-save list opens faster.
- Pickers show when their list from the game data could not be read.
- Each Settings page's Reset says what it puts back, and puts back only that page's settings.
- Library folders are kept when settings are reset.
- Reloading or updating Poser no longer leaves the old copy of Poser in memory.
